newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso pares gains ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso pares gains ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: The Mexican peso ceded some ground gained in earlier trade by the close on Tuesday when some dealers buying back dollars they had sold in order to hedge against possible fallout from U.S. inflation data due out early on Wednesday.
"Brokers covered short dollar positions in case (U.S. economic) data left to come are bad," a trader said.

The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart both ended just 0.3 of a centavo firmer, at 7.9060/7.9090 and 7.9030/7.9060 per dollar, respectively. The 48-hour peso had firmed to 7.8980/7.9010 at mid-morning trade.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.3 centavos firmer at 7.9020/7.9050 per dollar.

"The peso opened strong in response to U.S. retail sales data, which were seen as reducing the possibility of hikes in U.S. interest rates," the trader added, referring to the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rate policy.
Dealers added that expected increases in domestic interest rates bolstered the peso in late trade.
"Some dealers stayed short on dollars due to forecasts for the Cetes auction," another trader said.

A Reuters survey nN13531118 of nine money market dealers showed they forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at an average of 19.37 percent later in the day. This would be an increase of 76 basis points since last week's auction.
Banco de Mexico is expected to release the results of its weekly auction of government securities at 1830/2330 GMT.
